items.title: Hitler nearly walked out of the Nazi Party in 1921
items.claim: In July 1921, Hitler threatened to resign from the NSDAP unless he was given dictatorial control. What happened?

options.text: He was expelled and founded a rival party
The committee accepted his terms by a vote of 543 to 1 — the lone dissenter being a printer named Posch
He was forced to share leadership with Anton Drexler
The party split in two, with Hitler taking the Munich faction

items.reveal:
Anton Drexler had founded the German Workers' Party in 1919. Hitler joined in September 1919 as member 555 (the numbering started at 500 to inflate membership). By 1921 he was the party's most effective speaker.

When Drexler tried to merge with another nationalist group, Hitler resigned in protest, then demanded the chairmanship with dictatorial powers as the price of returning. The 29 July 1921 vote went 543 to 1.
items.why: Hitler's rise feels inevitable in hindsight. In 1921 he was a fringe agitator in a fringe party negotiating his way to control of an organisation with no national presence. Contingency, again.

items.title: The Great Pyramid was the world's tallest building for 3,800 years
items.claim: How tall is the Great Pyramid and how long did it hold the height record?

options.text: Originally around 146.7 m (now around 138.5 m after loss of casing stones), built around 2560 BCE for Pharaoh Khufu — the tallest human structure until Lincoln Cathedral's spire (around 160 m) in 1311 CE
It has been the world's tallest building continuously

items.reveal:
The Great Pyramid of Giza was built during the Fourth Dynasty for Khufu (Greek: Cheops). It contains around 2.3 million blocks averaging 2.5 tonnes each. The construction took perhaps 20 years using rotating labour gangs (around 20,000-30,000 workers at peak).

Lincoln Cathedral's central spire (completed around 1311) finally exceeded it. That spire collapsed in 1549. The Eiffel Tower (1889) finally and permanently dethroned the pyramid as the world's tallest human structure.

The original outer casing of polished white Tura limestone was largely removed in medieval Cairo for building material — including for the Hassan Mosque (1356).
items.why: Scale matters in human achievement. A building completed 4,500 years ago held the height record for 3,800 of those years — a testament to ancient engineering that modern construction took until the 19th century to surpass.

items.title: Harold won the first battle of 1066 — then lost the second three weeks later
items.claim: King Harold Godwinson fought two major battles in 1066. What happened?

options.text: Hastings was his only battle of the year
He defeated Harald Hardrada and Tostig at Stamford Bridge on 25 September, then marched 250 miles south and lost to William at Hastings on 14 October
He won at Hastings but died of wounds soon after
He defeated William at Hastings, then was killed by Harald Hardrada

items.reveal:
Harald Hardrada of Norway and Harold's exiled brother Tostig landed in Yorkshire in September 1066. Harold marched north and crushed them at Stamford Bridge on 25 September — Hardrada and Tostig were killed.

Three days later William of Normandy landed at Pevensey. Harold's exhausted army marched south and met William at Senlac Hill near Hastings on 14 October. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records Harold's death; the Bayeux Tapestry depicts a figure with an arrow to the eye, though the identification is debated.
items.why: The Conquest is taught as a single event. It was actually a year of crisis with two invasions, one of which Harold won. Without Stamford Bridge weakening his army, Hastings might have gone the other way.
